review_rounds.harness_note: Roles were told v0.31.2 had just shipped and to judge 0.32.0 against the current tree rather than the tree it was drafted against, with a list of what changed. implementer was given five load-bearing claims to verify against real code; tester was given the existing test files; ax-economist was told 0.31.2 enlarged the per-role prompt cost this feature lets a project decline.

Roles were told the spec was rewritten rather than patched (treat as a new document), given the old->new section renumbering, and each asked to re-examine the change their own round-1 high drove: architect on whether deleting the old trim_candidate section leaves §1's cited complaint unanswered, ax-economist on whether §1.1's arithmetic overstates the saving, implementer on five load-bearing code claims, tester on the 16 test items.

Roles were asked to re-derive the changes their own round-2 highs drove, and two were asked pointed questions about whether my fix opened a new door: architect on whether the --no-state carve-out makes the guard optional in practice, ax-economist on whether §2.6's doubled length is the feature's complexity or the tree's.

Two changes since round 3: §2.6's refusal was cut to a warning, and the spec was compressed 50% (3386 -> 1677 words) by removing rationale prose while keeping every requirement. Roles were told the removal was deliberate and instructed NOT to report 'the spec no longer explains why' — only lost requirements. regression was told the compression is the change most likely to have broken something.

Round-4 repairs were deliberately minimal (+154 words). Roles were told rationale removal was intentional and instructed not to report 'no longer explains why'. architect was asked whether stating the --quiet gap resolves or merely discloses the advisory-as-safeguard problem, and what happens when spec-coverage is deactivated; ax-economist was asked whether the shrunken feature is still worth shipping and to justify it in savings.

Roles were told §2.6's guard was removed entirely (its claim was false: ReviewRoundClean is per-round) and that deactivating spec-coverage is now refused. architect was asked to hunt the recurring 'promises a protection tp does not perform' pattern; regression was told a removal is the highest-risk diff.

regression was asked to verify every round-6 resolution claim against the spec text, after round 5 recorded four findings as fixed against an edit never made. ax-economist was told returning zero findings is a valid answer.

regression was asked to verify round 7's per-index resolutions against the spec text and report any whose edit was absent; it confirmed all ten highs held and found residue in the mediums. Three roles were told zero findings is a valid answer at this stage.
regression was asked to verify round 8's per-index resolutions and to check nothing contradicts the new buffering rule; three roles were told zero findings is a valid answer.

round 9's item-15 repair was a str.replace whose anchor did not match; it silently no-opped and was recorded fixed anyway. Round 10's repair script asserts every anchor is present and unique before replacing.
